name: Hex Tile Cartogram
summary: A newsroom hex tile map where Pulse lights every region and one tile's coral drop spreads to its neighbours.
look: Warm paper, equal hexagons with paper gutters, a strict 5-step coral↔teal ramp legend and mono tile codes. Election-night graphic energy, calm when all is teal.

components.name: Hex tile
components.role: equal-area region with 4 px paper gutters

components.name: Ramp legend
components.role: 5-step diverging key, coral ↔ teal, mono end labels

components.name: Tile code
components.role: short mono code inside the hot tile (W2)

components.name: Leader line
components.role: ink elbow from the hot tile to the explanation

components.name: Ring ripple
components.role: colour wave spreading by hex distance

components.name: Decision strip
components.role: rule, −18%, context and the two actions

motion.name: Tile flip
motion.how: each hex rotates Y 180° with power2.inOut 0.25 s (8th note at 120 BPM), colour swaps at the midpoint

motion.name: Ring ripple
motion.how: rings keyed by hex distance, delay = ring × 0.5 s so each ring hits a beat

motion.name: Contagion
motion.how: hot tile flips on the snare, neighbours follow at +0.25 s and +0.5 s with a 1.06 scale pulse, sine.out

story: Hook: a hex map in nine random colours with one coral tile nobody sees. Drop: the map flips grey and teal rings ripple out from the Acme mark in the centre hex. Proof: checkout conversion by region, W2 turns coral and spreads, −18% since 09:42 after deploy #2231, Roll back. CTA: a calm teal cluster, Every metric. Every minute., Start free.
adapt: Tile whatever your product has many of (regions, stores, services, customers, devices) into an equal-size hex grid; the anomaly is the tile that flips and starts to spread.

references.note: NPR on why equal hex tiles beat choropleths for quick reads

fit.risk: Hex maps imply geography; if your product has no regions, relabel tiles as services or customers or the metaphor confuses.
